title: A Ledger for the Confession
premise: Bram Blackwood, the reclusive coroner of Hollow Creek, has spent a decade solving quietly what the county police dismiss, keeping her gift hidden to protect her fragile place in a town that distrusts outsiders. When a confession to a thirty-year-old death arrives postmarked the day after the victim's funeral, the letter's author claims the statute of limitations is about to expire and dares Bram to prove it. Her investigation entwines her with Elias Marsh, the deceased's estranged son and the one man whose alibi she must break, forcing a choice between duty and a love that makes her want to stop being invisible. In the end, Bram exposes a cover-up protected by the town's founding families, but chooses mercy over prosecution, and in doing so finally claims a belonging she never believed she'd earned.
about_author: Wendell Nystrom is a former small-town records clerk who spent fifteen years cataloguing deaths, deeds, and disappearances in rural county archives. His novels are known for their patient, forensic intimacy and their affection for communities that keep their secrets in ledgers rather than words.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Bram tends the funeral of Ada Voss, the third 'accidental' death she's quietly doubted, walking the cemetery where she knows every grave by name. The town's polite coldness toward her underscores her isolation. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into resolve as she decides, once more, to investigate alone.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: POV Bram. A day after Ada's burial, a letter arrives confessing to a 1995 drowning ruled accidental, signed only 'A debtor,' and postmarked Hollow Creek. Bram realizes the writer knew Ada's funeral date. Emotional beat: unease curdling into fascination as the case becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Marsh Alibi
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Bram traces the drowned man, Thomas Voss, and finds his estranged son Elias Marsh holds the only alibi for the night of the death, sworn by three founding families. Their first meeting crackles with mutual suspicion and unwanted attraction. Emotional beat: duty and desire colliding at the doorstep.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Digging through county archives, Bram finds a page razored from the 1995 coroner's ledger, and discovers her own predecessor signed off under pressure. She realizes the cover-up has roots deeper than one night. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by the cost of knowing.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Bram and Elias, uneasy allies now, search the riverbank where Thomas died and find a corroded watch engraved with a name that isn't his. Someone else was there that night. Emotional beat: tentative trust, the first warmth she's allowed herself in years.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Bram interviews the aging patriarchs of Hollow Creek, whose alibis for each other are word-for-word identical, rehearsed thirty years ago. One slips, mentioning a detail only the killer would know. Emotional beat: dread as the town's beloved facade begins to crack.

chapters.title: A Debt in Ink
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Bram identifies the letter's handwriting: Ada Voss herself wrote it before dying, carrying a debt she could no longer hold. The confession was inheritance, passed to Bram deliberately. Emotional beat: grief braided with fury, as the victim becomes her co-investigator from beyond the grave.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Bram. The statute expires at midnight. Bram reconstructs the night: Thomas discovered the families' embezzled trust fund, and his death was ordered by the man Elias calls uncle, the town's patriarch, who confesses privately, believing himself untouchable. Emotional beat: the vertigo of holding absolute truth with no legal power to use it.

chapters.title: The Confession Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Climax. Bram publishes the reconstructed ledger at the town hall meeting, forcing the patriarch's public collapse and the families' mutual betrayals. Elias, implicated by proximity, stands to lose everything, and Bram must choose between the clean case and the man. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided in front of the whole town.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Resolution. Bram chooses mercy for Elias and lets the surviving families rot in exposure rather than prison, then carves Thomas Voss's true story into the record. At the cemetery, the town finally greets her by name. Emotional beat: belonging earned, love accepted, the invisible woman made visible.
